title: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management: billing meter change for non-Microsoft 365 AI retention
summary: Pass with two minor corrections: extend the retention-policy wizard path to the location selector and flag the existing AI retention locations as preview. The billing claims match the roadmap and Learn, with unpublished migration details appropriately left open. Instructions in the historical verification comment were ignored as evidence and directions.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management retains and deletes content.
claims.quote: Ready to start managing the lifecycle of your organization's data by retaining the content that you need to keep, and deleting the content that you don't?

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft plans a DLM billing meter change for non-Microsoft 365 generative AI prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Data Lifecycle Management (DLM) billing will be based on the volume of data retained.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Customers will need to migrate from the legacy meter to the new meter.
claims.quote: Customers will need to migrate from the legacy meter to the new meter.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes retained non-Microsoft 365 AI data priced at $0.25 per GB per month.
claims.quote: 1 GB of retained data will be billed at $0.25 per GB per month

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap gives an approximate daily equivalent of $0.0082 per GB.
claims.quote: (equivalent to ~$0.0082 per GB per day)

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The roadmap also describes billing based on the total volume of text messages managed by a DLM policy.
claims.quote: In the updated model, DLM is billed based on the total volume of text messages managed by a DLM policy.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Each non-Microsoft 365 generative AI prompt and response is an individual text message in the planned model.
claims.quote: Each non-Microsoft 365 generative AI prompt and response is treated as an individual text message

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap gives a rate equivalent to $6 per one million managed text messages in storage per month.
claims.quote: Billing is calculated on the managed text messages in storage, at a rate equivalent to $6 per one million text messages per month.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment / Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The item describes a billing change while prompts and responses remain retained and deleted according to configured Purview retention settings.
claims.quote: Each non-Microsoft 365 generative AI prompt and response is treated as an individual text message and is retained and deleted according to the configured Microsoft Purview retention settings.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance / After rollout; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft's analysis expects the overall cost impact to be cost-neutral or lower.
claims.quote: Based on current analysis, the overall cost impact is expected to be cost-neutral or lower for customers under the new billing model.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap supplies both byte-based and message-based pricing descriptions without explaining their relationship.
claims.quote: 1 GB of retained data will be billed at $0.25 per GB per month (equivalent to ~$0.0082 per GB per day). In the updated model, DLM is billed based on the total volume of text messages managed by a DLM policy.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance / Before rollout
claims.claim: Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy opens the relevant wizard in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy > Assign admin units > Full directory > Choose the type of retention policy to create > Static > Choose locations to apply the policy', the documented static-policy route at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-retention-policies. The current path correctly opens the wizard but stops before its location selector.

New-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy

The Applications parameter specifies the applications to include in the policy.
